channel.title: Communications Earth & Environment
channel.description:
Communications Earth & Environment is an open access journal from Nature Portfolio that publishes high-quality research, reviews and commentary in the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. The papers we publish represent significant advances that bring new insight to a specialized area of research. We also provide a community forum for issues of importance to Earth, environmental and planetary scientists, regardless of sub-discipline.

Our scope covers all areas of the geosciences, climate and environmental sciences as well as planetary sciences, including those at the interface with ecology, sustainability and environmental social sciences. Primary research of interest to the journal includes important insights gained from field work, novel analyses of existing data, numerical or analytical modelling, theoretical studies or laboratory experiments.

We encourage submissions that provide independent confirmation of particularly influential publications.

The submission and review processes are managed by our in-house professional editors supported by our Editorial Board Members, who provide technical expertise across the breadth of the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. We are committed to rapid dissemination of important research results. Articles are published on a continuous basis to ensure swift communication of findings.

item.title: Cascading fishery collapse associated with thermal habitat degradation, marine heatwaves, and predator influx
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04110-w

Early-summer La Niña conditions amplify marine heatwaves that are contributing to the collapse of the Japanese flying squid fishery and increasing the risk of a zero-catch state by the 2040 s, according to multi-decadal observations and climate projections.
item.dc:title: Cascading fishery collapse associated with thermal habitat degradation, marine heatwaves, and predator influx

item.title: Herbaceous leaf hydraulic trade-offs shape ecosystem function across the Mongolian Plateau
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04121-7

A community-wide trade-off between hydraulic efficiency and safety shapes dryland ecosystem function, with efficiency promoting biomass but safety improving water-use efficiency and stability, based on hydraulic trait surveys across 306 sites along a Mongolian Plateau precipitation gradient.
item.dc:title: Herbaceous leaf hydraulic trade-offs shape ecosystem function across the Mongolian Plateau

item.title: Climate warming amplifies coastal hypoxia response to extreme river discharge
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04106-6

Climate-driven extreme river discharge is projected to prolong and intensify coastal hypoxia, with stronger stratification and spatially uneven oxygen loss, suggests a study using an event-based storyline framework with a 3D hydrodynamic-biogeochemical model applied to the Ariake Sea, Japan.
item.dc:title: Climate warming amplifies coastal hypoxia response to extreme river discharge

item.title: Insect outbreak progression over three years shapes biogenic volatile emissions in a mountain birch forest
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03920-2

Increasing damage from geometrid moths in mountain birch forests led to higher emissions of volatile organic compounds and altered their composition in subarctic Sweden, as shown by three years of in situ measurements during a natural moth outbreak progression.
item.dc:title: Insect outbreak progression over three years shapes biogenic volatile emissions in a mountain birch forest

item.title: Circularity measures enhance resilience of net zero pathways for agriculture
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04052-3

In Ireland, circular bioeconomy strategies modestly reduce climate impact but markedly improve the country’s resilience by reducing dependence on imported inputs, according to integrated modelling of 12 sustainability indicators.
item.dc:title: Circularity measures enhance resilience of net zero pathways for agriculture

item.title: Seasonal predictability of spring solar resources and wind-solar variability across the United States
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04114-6

Spring solar resources can be reliably predicted across the United States Southwest, with skillful wind-solar variability forecasts and key climate drivers identified, according to a state-of-the-art seasonal forecast system and predictability analysis.
item.dc:title: Seasonal predictability of spring solar resources and wind-solar variability across the United States

item.title: Future methane measurement campaigns require basin-specific sampling strategies
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04089-4

The presence of super-emitters in oil and gas basins can influence sample size requirements when estimating methane emissions, according to data analyses from six US oil and gas basins.
item.dc:title: Future methane measurement campaigns require basin-specific sampling strategies

Dorit M. Hammerling

item.title: Aridity-driven shifts in plant–microbial diversity relationships across the arid and semi-arid grasslands of northern China
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 03 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04127-1

Increasing aridity drives taxon-specific biodiversity thresholds in northern Chinese grasslands, reducing plant, bacterial, and fungal diversity while increasing archaeal species diversity and restructuring plant-microbe coupling, based on a field survey across arid and semi-arid regions.
item.dc:title: Aridity-driven shifts in plant–microbial diversity relationships across the arid and semi-arid grasslands of northern China
